Date · 25 Jun 2026

What this sheet is

Nine first-pass renderings of the logo direction you already chose in Part 2 — a hand-drawn signature wordmark, with the record-groove icon and the “written → crossed-out → final” motif explored around it. These are starting points, not final art: AI drafts to react to. The one(s) you point at get redrawn vector-clean by hand and built into the full system (favicon, reversed, mono, lockups).

They’re deliberately spread across a spectrum — from the most restrained (Aesop-quiet) to the loosest (brush-pen energy) — so you can feel where on the line “The Long Play” should sit. Everything stays in the brand palette and refuses the two traps the brief names: glossy-corporate and cute-childish.

Palette 1 “Field & Studio” — green · cream · muted gold · ink, with moss / brick semantics.

The rules these obey

  • ✓ One person’s hand — a musician’s autograph, not a typeface.
  • ✓ Adult & confident — restraint carries the prestige.
  • ✓ Rough & real — visible line-weight, anti-AI, pro-craft.
  • ✕ No bouncy “kids’ classroom” letters.
  • ✕ No glossy SaaS / stock-premium gloss.
  • ✕ The crossed-out motif never touches the logo itself.
A

The signature, across the spectrum

Same words, five registers — from whisper-quiet to brush-loud. This is the core decision: how much “hand” do you want?

LEAD

01 · The Signature

Fine-liner · ink on cream

The plumb-centre of the direction: a single confident hand, fine ink line, warm cream ground. Reads grown-up and personal — a record sleeve signed, not a logo designed.

Why it leads: closest to “Akshit’s own hand” (§9) without tipping cute or loud. Safest distinctiveness-to-legibility balance.

SPECTRUM

02 · The Quiet One

Hairline · apothecary restraint

The most understated end — thin, spacious, intellectual. The Aesop register. Says “premium” through silence rather than flourish.

Watch: the hairline can get fragile small & on signage — it’s the elegant risk-edge of the range.

SPECTRUM

03 · The Brush

Brush-pen · forest green

Loudest, most energetic cut — visible brush weight, the green leading. More “indie label” than “studio”. The most ownable, the most opinionated.

Watch: the strongest character, but the furthest from quiet — sits opposite #02 on the dial.

B

The mark you can shrink

A signature dies at favicon size — so the system needs an extracted icon. The “long play” pun and the favicon problem solve each other.

COMBINATION

04 · Signature + Groove

Lockup · word + record mark

The full combination: the wordmark with a small concentric record-groove set to its left. One lockup that carries both the name and the meaning of the name.

Solves: the favicon gap (Step 6) — the groove is the part that survives small.

ICON

05 · The Groove

Icon only · 1-colour

The mark on its own — concentric grooves of an LP. Doubles as the “long play” pun and the avatar / app-icon / emboss. Holds at 32px where the signature can’t.

Provocation: what if the record is the brand mark — the name’s meaning becomes the logo?

REVERSED

06 · On Green

Reversed · cream on forest

The dark-ground variant — cream signature on deep green, for packaging, dark web sections, the record-sleeve mood. Confirms the mark survives inverted.

System note: every chosen mark needs this reversed cut + a bold mono cut for thermal/emboss.

C

The motif & the lockups

Where “The Long Play” lives in the wild — the ownable “shown-working” device, plus the stacked and poster compositions.

MOTIF

07 · Shown Working

Device · draft → final

Your “written → crossed-out → final” idea as a system device, not a logo: a word struck through, the better word beside it. For headlines, dividers, motion — “lessons” becomes “relationship”.

Rule: lives in headlines & animation only — never on the logo or small sizes (it reads as an error there).

LOCKUP

08 · Stacked Lockup

Icon · word · tagline

The vertical lockup for social cards, tags and signage: groove above, signature, tagline beneath in the warm serif. The full identity in one square.

Type pairing: Fraunces (warm serif) + Inter — both free/OFL, zero licensing friction.

HERO

09 · The Hero

Poster · website lead

The website-hero / manifesto composition — wordmark large, tagline set clean beneath, gold rule. Tests whether the name + tagline can carry a cold parent who doesn’t know the brand yet.

Provocation: for cold parents, does the tagline deserve to be the hero, with the name small beneath?

What we need from you

Don’t pick a finished logo — react. Point at what feels like you and what doesn’t. The picks get redrawn by hand; these are only the conversation.

1 · The register
  • Where on the dial — Quiet (#02), Signature (#01), or Brush (#03)?
  • Ink-black, or green-led?
  • Does any of them feel like your own hand?
2 · The mark
  • Is the record-groove (#05) the right icon — or too literal?
  • Signature alone, or always with the groove (#04)?
  • Should the record be the logo?
3 · The motif
  • Does “shown working” (#07) feel ownable or gimmicky?
  • Name-led or tagline-led hero (#09)?
  • Anything here you’d rule out cold?
